questions.stem: Find the pH of a $0.001\ \text{M}$ aqueous solution of $\text{HCl}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$ (assume complete dissociation).
The pH of a $10^{-8}\ \text{M}$ aqueous $\text{HCl}$ solution at $25^\circ\text{C}$ is closest to

options.whyWrong: An acid can't give a basic pH. Water's $\text{H}^+$ was ignored.
Adding acid must lower the pH slightly below 7.
This would need $[\text{H}^+] = 10^{-6}\ \text{M}$, ten times more than is present.

questions.solution:
**Key idea:** at this dilution water's own ionisation ($10^{-7}\ \text{M}$ of $\text{H}^+$) dominates, and the solution must still be (slightly) acidic.

1. $[\text{H}^+] = x$ with $x^2 - 10^{-8}x - 10^{-14} = 0$
2. $x \approx 1.05 \times 10^{-7}\ \text{M}$
3. **$\text{pH} \approx 6.98$**
hints: Compare $10^{-8}$ with the $[\text{H}^+]$ that pure water already has.
